Economic theories that have changed us: game theory

I just started learning Game Theory just this week. Bought the Game Theory 101 book on Amazon to start out but I don't really know where can I go from here. Do you have a recommendation for a book or a source that I can dig deeper into Game Theory? (most books I found on Amazon are expensive textbooks about the subject)

Sorry it took so long for me to get back to you on this. There is a wealth of information available for free on the web. This includes seminal books such as Von Neuman's 'Theory of Games and Economic Behavior', John Maynard Smith's 'Evolution and the Theory of Games' as well as introductions such as 'Introduction to Game Theory' by Christian Jolmi, 'Essentials of Game Theory: A Concise Multidisciplinary Introduction' by Leyton, Brown and Shoroom and 'Games and Information: An Introduction to Game Theory' by Eric Rasmussen.

It's hard for me to give precise recommendations given that I don't know about your present interests (mathematics, biology, economics, computer science, political science, sociology, psychology and so on and so on) nor your mathematical background. College textbook publishing is an old and much criticized scam. What I can suggest is going to the Wikipedia page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_theory) and head down to the 'Notes', 'References' and especially the 'Websites' sections. I think that everything I have listed above is also listed there, along with so much more. Given what is available for free I see no need for you to pay a penny.

Take care and good luck.
